palette.notes: Advice only: start animating with small sprites, limited palettes and clear colour separation.

silhouette: Keyframes must read on their own: a punch reads from wind-up and full extension alone; run strides need extended limbs and a forward tilt.

motion.timing: Article's example: 8-frame run at 80 ms per pose, cut to 4 frames at 160 ms per pose; 6-frame run is his usual sweet spot; Mega Man run: 3 poses in a 4-frame loop. Article figures, not measured.

texture: Loops expose every stray pixel; check clusters on every frame.

acting.acts: Idle must simply move: a bouncy breathing loop is the common choice; 8-bit JRPGs reuse a 2-frame walk as idle. Keep idle length consistent across characters to fit the budget.

techniques: 3-pose run: stride, pass, stride with the pass frame reused in a 4-frame loop
when cutting frames, drop recoil first, then the high point; never contact or pass
double the frame duration when halving the frame count (80 ms x8 -> 160 ms x4)
check every frame for stray pixels before looping
feel: few strong key poses + held longer + small bounce = energetic motion without sluggish smoothness
for_fred: Give Fred a 2-frame breathing idle and a short swim cycle built from 3-4 strong key poses held around 80-160 ms, and spend the frames saved on acting beats (exit, return, background cameo) instead of looping the same smooth animation; reuse one idle rhythm for Fred and Pixie so they feel like one world.
